title: fix(cuda-graph): shape-guard-aware graph cache keying and warmup regression fix
author: Markus Chen
description:
Context: Recent CUDA graph capture/replay work introduced shape guards to support dynamic sequence lengths (see prior PRs: #18345, #18712, #19023). A perf-canary flagged a regression where warmup runs were not matching the graph cache keys produced during normal inference due to missing shape-guard inclusion in the cache key. This caused graph misses during steady-state and manifested as higher tail latency and lower throughput for certain workloads.

What this PR does: Adds shape-guard-aware graph cache keying, improves warmup generation to create representative guarded graphs, and reintroduces a conservative fallback path for unknown/unseen shapes. The change is gated behind a runtime feature flag (runtime.use_shape_guard_keys) and includes unit/integration tests plus a microbenchmark.

Key changes: 
- Include shape-guard fingerprint (serialized guard ranges + dtype) in cuda_graph cache key computation.
- Extend the warmup generator to emit guarded capture traces for the top-N observed sequence length buckets (configurable, default N=3) so that common variants are pre-captured.
- Add a fast-path in the executor to match replayable graphs by shape-guard first, falling back to previous heuristic matching if no guarded graph exists.
- Add extensive logging and metrics (cuda_graph.cache_hit{guarded,ungarded}, cuda_graph.warmup_captures) for easier debugging and SRE diagnostics.
- Add feature flag runtime.use_shape_guard_keys (off by default for a short canary period).

Why: This fixes a real production regression where graphs captured during warmup did not match runtime request shapes, preventing reuse of captured graphs and increasing both GPU kernel dispatch overhead and CPU scheduling. By aligning warmup captures with the guarded graph keying used at replay time, we restore expected capture/replay hit rates and reduce latency and GPU utilization.

Testing and results: 
- Unit tests for guard serialization and cache key determinism.
- Integration test exercising warmup followed by synthetic workload with mixed sequence lengths.
- Microbenchmarks on c4-small perf-canary: guarded graph hit rate increased from ~62% to ~95% for observed traffic pattern; median token latency reduced by ~12%, p99 reduced by ~18%; throughput improved ~22% in our continuous-batching testing harness.

Rollout plan: 
- Ship behind runtime.use_shape_guard_keys flag. Enable for perf-canary cluster for 48 hours. Validate metrics (cache_hit ratio, token latency, warmup capture counts). Gradually flip on for more clusters if stable.

Additional notes: 
- This PR keeps fallback behavior to avoid correctness risks for very unusual shapes. 
- Documented the new feature flag and metrics in the runtime observability section. 

Checklist: 
- [x] Add shape-guard fingerprinting to cache key. 
- [x] Warmup generator changes and config knobs. 
- [x] Tests and microbenchmarks. 
- [x] Metrics and logging. 
- [x] Feature flag and rollout docs.

Related: linked Linear tickets ENG-4567 (investigate graph warmup regression), ENG-4620 (improve warmup diversity), SUP-1029 (customer report: increased latency after recent cuda-graph merge).

review_comments: Priya Menon: Can you explain why we need to include dtype in the guard key? I thought dtype was stable across captures.

Markus Chen: Dtype is usually stable but mixed-precision paths can change (float16 vs float32) depending on operator kernels and compilation path; including dtype prevents replay mismatch and avoids subtle kernel selection regressions.
Carlos Ortega: Please add a short-circuit to avoid allocating guard vectors for tiny requests (cost vs benefit).
Markus Chen: Added short-circuit in warmup and executor; note included in commits c2e7a9f and d88f2b3.
Ava Liu: CI flaked on the first run due to an unrelated linter change; re-ran and all checks passed.
Priya Menon: Approved after addressing the guard key determinism test failures.
release_notes: Fix: Ensure cuda-graph cache keys incorporate shape guards and improve warmup capture diversity to restore capture/replay hit rates and reduce latency. Feature gated and rolled out via runtime.use_shape_guard_keys.
notes_for_sre: Enable runtime.use_shape_guard_keys on perf-canary first. Monitor metrics: cuda_graph.cache_hit{guarded,ungarded}, cuda_graph.warmup_captures, token_latency_p99. The fallback path will keep latency bounded for unseen shapes.
